content:
The only way to split 5 tickets into 4 nonempty consecutive blocks is to have one block of 2 consecutive tickets and three single tickets.

The possible consecutive 2-ticket blocks are:
\[
(1,2), (2,3), (3,4), (4,5)
\]
So there are \(4\) possible block partitions.

Each partition into 4 blocks can be assigned to the 4 distinct people in \(4!\) ways.

\[
4 \times 4! = 4 \times 24 = 96
\]

\boxed{96}
